editorial:
Imagine being a vampire who is just too nice to actually hunt people. That is the spot Sasha finds herself in. She is a total sweetheart who hates the idea of hurting anyone, which really annoys her parents. When they finally stop giving her blood to force her to grow up, she is basically starving. That is when she meets Paul, a lonely kid who actually wants to end his life. It sounds dark, but the movie plays it as a quirky, sweet comedy. You get to follow these two oddballs as they make a deal: he lets her eat, and she helps him check off his bucket list before he goes. It is a weirdly cozy movie that feels like a late-night walk through a quiet city.

The chemistry between the two leads is the best part of the whole experience. You can tell they really like each other, which makes the emotional parts hit harder. The pacing is steady, though some might find the slow moments a bit too long. If you like stories about unlikely friendships and dark humor, you will love this.
endingExplained: After spending the night together, Paul realizes that he actually wants to live because of the connection he found with Sasha. Sasha decides she cannot kill him because she cares for him too much. Instead of a tragedy, they choose to find a way to survive together. They move past their sadness and decide to face the future as friends, proving that finding someone who understands you is the best cure for loneliness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird romances and dark comedies.
